subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which British Commander was defeated by the Santhals in 1855?
explanation: The Santhals were given land and persuaded to settle in the foothills of Rajmahal. By 1832 AD, a large area of land was demarcated as Damin-i-Koh. This was declared to be the land of the Santhals. After the demarcation of Damin-i-Koh, Santhal settlements expanded rapidly. As cultivation expanded, an increased volume of revenue flowed into the Company’s coffers. The Santhals, however soon found that the land they had brought under cultivation was slipping away from their hands. The state was levying heavy taxes on the land that the Santhals had cleared, moneylenders (dikkus) were charging them high rates of interest and taking over the land when debts remained unpaid, and zamindars were asserting control over the Damin area. It was after the Santhal Revolt (1855-56) that the Santhal Pargana was created, carving out 5,500 square miles from the districts of Bhagalpur and Birbhum. On 30 June 1855, two Santhal rebel leaders, Siddhu and Kanhu Murmu, mobilized ten thousand Santhals and declared a rebellion against British colonists. In the five-hour bloody struggle, Santhals near Bhagalpur had defeated Major Burrough.
source: Modern India GS · Modern India GS p.50

explanation: The Sanyasi rebellion took place during the period of 1770-80 AD at Bengal. The terrible famine in Bengal in 1770 AD caused this province to suffer from chaos and misery. On other hand, the restrictions imposed on the pilgrimage made the Sanyasis very upset that they revolted against the British rule. The description of Sanyasi rebellion can be found in the famous book of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, ‘Anand Math’. Kol revolt (1831-1832) was widely spread over the region of Ranchi, Hazaribagh, Singhbhum, Palamau and western parts of Manbhumi. The main cause of the Kol rebellion was the exploitation and oppression faced by the locals at the hands of other non-tribals. The local tribes were looked down upon and they also found the non-tribals, zamindars and other British agents encroaching their territories and threatening their dominance. The Kols thus rose in rebellion against the government officers, merchants and money lenders.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The system of indirect election was introduced in India in the year-
explanation: Indian Councils Act, 1892 was passed by the British Parliament to increase the size of the Legislative Councils. This Act marks the beginning of representative form of Government in India. The Act of 1892 can be said to be a first step towards the beginning of the representative government in India. However such representation was via only indirect elections and there was nothing for a common Indian. The system of indirect election prevented direct contact between the public and the representatives. The provisions of Act of 1892 were- (i) A system of indirect elections was introduced to elect the members of the councils. The universities, district board, municipalities, zamindars and chambers of commerce were empowered to recommend members to provincial councils. (ii) The power of the legislative councils was increased. The members could now discuss the budget without right to vote on it. They were also not allowed to ask supplementary questions. (iii) Governor General was empowered to fill the seat in the case of Central legislature and by the Governor in the case of provincial legislature.
source: Modern India GS · Modern India GS p.271
